note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 5198 / 出力 2314 トークン

data.question: Should the town adopt hold_limit 70s now as the first leg of a sequenced block_k=2 package, re-examine block_k=2 against the 1-2 company vote, or keep v1 while a procedure for measuring block_k=2 together with a sanction change is defined?
data.background: In D3 you asked for block_k=2 and a sanction change to be measured together, but the constitution allows only one parameter, one step, per amendment. Whether a sequenced package satisfies your condition is a question about how the regulation is read, so I cannot decide it. Option 1 is also worse for customers, who do not vote, and option 2 has again lost the company vote 1-2. Both are governance and customer-impact judgments that belong to you.

options.summary: Adopt hold_limit 60s → 70s. It passes check and the constitution and wins the vote (A ×, B ○, C ○), but it makes every measure worse. On-time falls from 264.6 to 260.6 (-4.0, 1/5 seeds improved). Late rises from 10.0 to 14.0. p95_wait_s rises from 121 to 141, and max_wait_s from 284 to 292. The lowest on-time rate falls from 0.93 to 0.89, and blocked s rises from 1855 to 2042. Road violations fall slightly, from 20.4 to 19.0. It does not even relieve the companies it is meant to help: utility falls for C (77.7 to 77.2) and B (80.3 to 79.9) as well as A (92.2 to 88.6). It commits nothing about the block_k=2 leg next period.
options.stakeholders: Customers lose: about 4 fewer on-time deliveries per run, and longer typical and worst-case waits. All three companies lose utility in this measurement, A the most. Nobody gains in the measured results. The only possible benefit is procedural: a path toward a later block_k=2 vote.

options.summary: Adopt block_k 3 → 2. This is the change you rejected in D1 to D3. On-time rises from 264.6 to 272.6 (+8.0, 5/5 seeds improved). Late falls from 10.0 to 2.0. p95_wait_s falls from 121 to 90.0, and max_wait_s from 284 to 212. The lowest on-time rate rises from 0.93 to 0.98, and blocked s falls from 1855 to 1102. Road violations rise from 20.4 to 29.6, with no per-company breakdown. It lost the vote (A ○, B ×, C ×), so adopting it would be the first override of a two-of-three majority.
options.stakeholders: Customers gain the most: faster and more reliable service. A gains utility (92.2 to 97.4). B loses (80.3 to 76.0), and C loses more (77.7 to 68.8), C being already the lowest-utility company. Road order worsens through the added violations, and who bears them is still unknown. Trust in the vote suffers if it is overridden.

options.summary: Stay at v1 (on-time 264.6, late 10.0, p95_wait_s 121, max_wait_s 284, unfinished 0.0). Separately, define a procedure that lets block_k=2 be measured and voted on jointly with a sanction change, together with the violation breakdown.
options.stakeholders: Customers forgo the +8.0 on-time gain and the shorter waits offered by option 2, but avoid the worsening in option 1. B and C keep their current utility. A forgoes the gain from block_k=2. The vote and the D1 to D3 conditions stay intact.

recommendation.reason: Option 1 is not a remedy. It worsens on-time (-4.0, 1/5 seeds), p95_wait_s (121 to 141) and max_wait_s, and it lowers the utility of C and B, the companies it was meant to relieve. A sequenced package does not bind the second leg, so customers could bear the cost of option 1 while block_k=2 still fails its vote. Option 2 still lacks the remedy for C and the violation breakdown you required, and it lost 1-2 again. Keeping v1 and authorising a joint-measurement procedure is the cleanest way to meet the D3 condition.
assumptions: The constitution's one-parameter, one-step rule cannot be satisfied by one amendment that changes block_k and a sanction parameter together.
The utility drop for B and C under hold_limit 70s also holds in other demand regimes, not only in this measurement.
The B and C votes against block_k=2 would not change without a sanction remedy.

unknowns: The per-company, per-type and per-severity breakdown of the added road violations under block_k=2 (20.4 to 29.6).
Whether B and C would vote for block_k=2 if it were paired with a sanction change, and their actual policies.
The combined effect of hold_limit 70s plus block_k=2 together, which has not been measured.
How customers perceive the longer waits under option 1.
Next period's demand regime, and whether the busy-regime results carry over.
Whether a constitutional amendment allowing joint multi-parameter proposals would be acceptable to the companies.
